Topics · The holy books together

Did Abraham and Moses teach what the Quran does?

The Quran says its message is in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses, and what stands there. Compare the list.

Part 1 of 3

﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَفِى ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ١٨ صُحُفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ١٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, The scriptures of Abraham and Moses.

Quran · Al-A'la 87:18-19

Translation

but the children of the murderers he didn’t put to death, according to that which is written in the book of the law of Moses, as Yahweh commanded, saying, “The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children be put to death for the fathers; but every man shall die for his own sin.”

Original · Hebrew

וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י הַמַּכִּ֖ים לֹ֣א הֵמִ֑ית כַּכָּת֣וּב בְּסֵ֣פֶר תּֽוֹרַת־מֹ֠שֶׁה אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹא־יוּמְת֨וּ אָב֤וֹת עַל־בָּנִים֙ וּבָנִים֙ לֹא־יוּמְת֣וּ עַל־אָב֔וֹת כִּ֛י אִם־אִ֥ישׁ בְּחֶטְא֖וֹ יוּמָֽת׃

2 Kings · 14:6

World English Bible

﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ١٤ وَذَكَرَ ٱسْمَ رَبِّهِۦ فَصَلَّىٰ١٥ بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا١٦ وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ١٧﴾

Translation of the meaning

He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself And mentions the name of his Lord and prays. But you prefer the worldly life, While the Hereafter is better and more enduring.

Quran · Al-A'la 87:14-17

Translation

Wash yourselves. Make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil.

Original · Hebrew

רַחֲצוּ֙ הִזַּכּ֔וּ הָסִ֛ירוּ רֹ֥עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם מִנֶּ֣גֶד עֵינָ֑י חִדְל֖וּ הָרֵֽעַ׃

Isaiah · 1:16

World English Bible

The Quran makes a claim that can be tested: this is in the earlier scrolls, those of Abraham and Moses. What is 'this'? The nearest reading points to the verses just before: whoever purifies the self, remembers the Lord's name and prays has prospered, and the life to come is better and more lasting. That is a claim about content. It names two men and says the same teaching stood with them. Anyone who holds the Torah can ask whether it stands there.

A question for you

What would you look for to test this claim?

If you sayThe same words.
ThenWords change between languages, and these books came in different tongues. The next part gives a sharper list.
If you sayThe same teaching.
ThenThat is what the verse claims, and the next part gives you something to compare.
If you sayAn old scroll of Abraham.
ThenThe Quran names those scrolls. What can be checked today is the teaching, in the books of Moses and those after.

Part 2 of 3

﴿أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِى صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ٣٦ وَإِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلَّذِى وَفَّىٰٓ٣٧ أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ٣٨ وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَـٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ٣٩ وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُۥ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ٤٠ ثُمَّ يُجْزَىٰهُ ٱلْجَزَآءَ ٱلْأَوْفَىٰ٤١﴾

Translation of the meaning

Or has he not been informed of what was in the scriptures of Moses And [of] Abraham, who fulfilled [his obligations] - That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another And that there is not for man except that [good] for which he strives And that his effort is going to be seen - Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense -

Quran · An-Najm 53:36-41

Translation

Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.

Original · Hebrew

וּלְךָֽ־אֲדֹנָ֥י חָ֑סֶד כִּֽי־אַתָּ֨ה תְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּֽמַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

the Psalms · 62:12

World English Bible

Another passage gives a list. Has he not been told what is in the scrolls of Moses, and of Abraham who fulfilled his pledge? Then it counts: no bearer carries another's load. A person has only what they strove for. Their striving will be seen. It will be repaid in full. This is specific, and it can be compared. The prophets of Israel say each soul carries its own deed, and the law of Moses says no one dies for another's sin. Read the two together.

A question for you

Which line of this list stops you most?

If you sayNo one carries another's load.
ThenA great line, and many prophets say it. Set it beside what you hold.
If you sayA person has only what they strove for.
ThenThen your small striving is counted, and none of it is lost.
If you sayTheir striving will be seen.
ThenThat is what everyone who toiled unseen has been waiting to hear.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَا يَأْتِينَا بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦٓ ۚ أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِم بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِى ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them evidence of what was in the former scriptures?[868]

Translator's notes

[868] Is not the Qur’ān an adequate proof of Muḥammad's prophethood and sufficient as a lasting miracle?

Quran · Ta-Ha 20:133

﴿وَإِنَّهُۥ لَفِى زُبُرِ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And indeed, it is [mentioned] in the scriptures of former peoples.

Quran · Ash-Shu'ara 26:196

Here is the boldest form of the claim. His opponents asked for a sign: why does he not bring us one from his Lord? The verse answers with a question: has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the earlier scrolls? They asked for a wonder and were pointed to an agreement. The sign on offer is that what he recites stands with what came before. Another verse says so plainly: it is in the writings of the ancients. You can look at that yourself.

A question for you

Which would persuade you more: a wonder, or an agreement you can check?

If you sayA wonder.
ThenMany asked for that. The Quran's answer is different, and wonders have their own Step.
If you sayAn agreement I can check.
ThenThen the next Step asks why the commands agree.
If you sayNeither yet.
ThenThat is fine. You can look at the one message the prophets carried.
